title: S$^2$GR: Stepwise Semantic-Guided Reasoning in Latent Space for Generative Recommendation

problem.claim: Generative recommendation methods primarily generate semantic IDs directly from interaction sequences, limiting deeper reasoning and performance potential.

gap.claim: Existing reasoning-enhanced generative recommendation approaches separate reasoning and generation sequentially, produce uninterpretable reasoning vectors, and rely on unverifiable supervision for reasoning paths.

contributions.claim: The authors propose S2GR, a stepwise semantic-guided reasoning framework for generative recommendation in latent space.

S2GR uses codebook optimization with item co-occurrence, load-balancing, and uniformity objectives to capture behavioral patterns, improve codebook utilization, and reinforce coarse-to-fine semantic hierarchies.
S2GR inserts thinking tokens before each semantic-ID generation step and supervises their coarse-grained semantics through contrastive learning against ground-truth codebook cluster distributions.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe S2GR's stepwise semantic-guided reasoning framework as novel and identify the stepwise reasoning mechanism as its core innovation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments demonstrating S2GR's superiority.
The authors report that an online A/B test confirmed efficacy on a large-scale industrial short video platform.

narrative_sequence.summary: Generative recommendation is presented as an emerging paradigm with end-to-end generation advantages.
Existing methods focus on direct semantic-ID generation and do not activate deeper reasoning capabilities.
Reasoning-enhanced approaches are described as having sequential separation, imbalanced computational focus, uninterpretable reasoning vectors, and unverifiable supervision.
S2GR combines optimized semantic codebooks with stepwise, contrastively supervised reasoning tokens before each semantic-ID generation step.
The authors report positive results from extensive experiments and an online A/B test.

source_observation.claim: The method places explicit reasoning tokens before each hierarchical semantic-ID generation step and supervises them using codebook cluster distributions.

interpretation.claim: Reasoning may become more aligned with hierarchical generation when intermediate representations are tied to explicit semantic targets.

application.claim: For hierarchical generation tasks, consider introducing interpretable intermediate tokens with supervision linked to the hierarchy's semantic structure.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this design transfers beyond generative recommendation or which supervision costs it introduces.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, metric values, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not provide quantitative details or statistical results for the online A/B test.
The abstract does not describe the unverifiable-supervision mechanism or its evaluation in detail.
